Definition
[Symmetric and strictly hyperbolic systems] ↗ def:hyperbolic-system 1. ch7:7.3.1-def-2\group Hyperbolic Systems

(i) We say (1) is a symmetric hyperbolic system if $B_j(x, t)$ is a symmetric $m \times m$ matrix for each $x \in \mathbb {R}^n$, $t \geq 0$ ($j = 1, \ldots , m$).

(ii) The system (1) is strictly hyperbolic if for each $x, y \in \mathbb {R}^n$, $y \neq 0$, and each $t \geq 0$, the matrix $\mathbf{B}(x, t; y)$ has $m$ distinct real eigenvalues: \[ \lambda _1(x, t; y) < \lambda _2(x, t; y) < \cdots < \lambda _m(x, t; y). \]
